jobs.description:
Head of Logistics Internal Transport ESK
 
Transport is at the core of modern society. Imagine using your expertise to shape sustainable transport and infrastructure solutions for the future. If you seek to make a difference on a global scale, working with next-gen technologies and the sharpest collaborative teams, then we could be a perfect match. 

About the role
As Head of Logistics Internal Transport, you will lead and develop the Internal Transport organization at our Eskilstuna factory, with an exciting opportunity to shape the next generation of internal logistics.
Leading approximately 30 employees, you will ensure reliable material flows and supply to machining and assembly operations, a vital part of keeping production running safely and efficiently.
 
This is a dynamic leadership role combining operational responsibility with strategic development. You will secure excellent daily operations while driving the transformation of internal logistics through continuous improvement, digitalization, automation, and Lean.
 
You will strengthen performance management through Lean principles, data-driven decisions, and fact-based priorities, turning insights into measurable improvements in safety, productivity, resource utilization, material flow, and quality.
As part of the Logistics Management Team, you will collaborate closely with Production, Supply Chain, Engineering, and other key stakeholders to identify opportunities, drive improvements, and shape the site's long-term development and strategy.

Who are you?
We are looking for a business-oriented and inspiring leader who is passionate about logistics, Lean, operational excellence, and developing people.
You know how to build high-performing teams through trust, collaboration, and clear expectations. You balance operational priorities with a long-term perspective and turn data and insights into actions that deliver real business results.
 
You thrive on collaboration, enjoy challenging existing ways of working, and know how to engage people in change and shared ambitions.
 
To succeed in this role, we believe you have:
A university degree in Industrial Engineering, Logistics, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Several years of leadership experience within logistics, manufacturing, operations, or supply chain.
A proven ability to lead and develop teams, creating engagement, accountability, and strong cross-functional collaboration.
A strong track record in productivity improvement, performance management, and continuous improvement through Lean principles and structured problemsolving.
Experience leading change and transformation initiatives.
Strong analytical skills and the ability to turn data into priorities, actions, and results.
Experience in digitalization and data-driven operational management is an advantage.
Fluency in Swedish and English, both spoken and written.

Are we a perfect match?
At Volvo CE, we believe diverse perspectives and inclusive teams create stronger business results. We welcome applicants with different backgrounds, experiences, and ways of thinking.
 
We cannot promise you an effortless job, but we can promise talented colleagues, exciting challenges, and the opportunity to make a real impact.
This is your opportunity to shape the future of Internal Transport. You will be at the heart of an exciting transformation journey, where automation, digitalization, data- driven decisions, and operational excellence will redefine how internal logistics supports tomorrow's production.
 
Join a global company with strong growth ambitions, where you can influence, innovate, and grow professionally while staying close to the operations where value is created every day.
 
Hiring Manager: Henrik Sohlen, henrik.sohlen@volvo.com
Last day to apply 13th of December
Location: On site Eskilstuna
As part of the recruitment process, a background check as well as alcohol and drug testing may be conducted. You will be informed if applicable. 

We value your data privacy and therefore do not accept applications via mail. 
 
Who we are and what we believe in 
We are committed to shaping the future landscape of efficient, safe, and sustainable transport solutions. Fulfilling our mission creates countless career opportunities for talents across the group’s leading brands and entities.
 
Applying to this job offers you the opportunity to join Volvo Group. Every day, you will be working with some of the sharpest and most creative brains in our field to be able to leave our society in better shape for the next generation. ​We are passionate about what we do, and we thrive on teamwork. ​We are almost 100,000 people united around the world by a culture of care, inclusiveness, and empowerment. 
 
Part of Volvo Group, Volvo Construction Equipment is a global company driven by our purpose to build the world we want to live in. Together we develop and deliver solutions for a cleaner, smarter, and more connected world. By unleashing everyone’s full potential, we build a more sustainable future for all our stakeholders. Come join our team and help us build a better tomorrow.

What we do
Kenvue is now part of Kimberly-Clark. Continue exploring opportunities at jobs.kenvue.com.
At Kenvue, we realize the extraordinary power of everyday care. Built on over a century of heritage and rooted in science, we’re the house of iconic brands - including NEUTROGENA®, AVEENO®, TYLENOL®, LISTERINE®, JOHNSON’S® and BAND-AID® that you already know and love. Science is our passion; care is our talent.
Who We Are
Our global team is ~ 22,000 brilliant people with a workplace culture where every voice matters, and every contribution is appreciated. We are passionate about insights, innovation and committed to delivering the best products to our customers. With expertise and empathy, being a Kenvuer means having the power to impact millions of people every day. We put people first, care fiercely, earn trust with science and solve with courage – and have brilliant opportunities waiting for you! Join us in shaping our future–and yours. What you will do
The Principal Scientist, Self Care Product Development is responsible for leading the definition, design, development, and execution of complex product initiatives aligned with brand and business strategy. This includes establishing project scope, performance targets, and rigorous problem-solving approaches while leveraging deep organizational and technical expertise. This role will contribute to gross profit (GP) optimization and advance embedded sustainability across product development activities.
This position provides R&D leadership and strong technical expertise throughout project execution, integrating human centered insights, robust experimentation, and data driven decision making. The Principal Scientist will collaborate closely across multifunctional teams—ensuring cohesive partnership, strategic alignment, and the successful translation of consumer and business needs into innovative, high quality selfcare solutions.
Project Leadership & Execution
Lead and own end to end technical execution of product development projects, including formulation, product design, process development, and scale-up activities, ensure full delivery of self-care R&D projects.
Define project pathways, ensure milestones remain on track, and independently drive technical problem solving.
Execute hands on experimental lab work, scaleup analysis, and pipeline activities as needed.
Partner with cross functional teams (Packaging, Commercial, Supply Chain, etc.) to align deliverables, resources, and project priorities.
Communicate project progress updates and ensure all work complies with internal and external standards (EHS, Quality, Medical, Regulatory).
Create and maintain all required development documentation and author technical reports and peer reviewed manuscripts.

Technical Expertise & Leadership
Provide deep expertise in formulation science, chemistry, and process understanding.
Optimize ingredient systems to meet cost, performance, and supply requirements.
Oversee daily laboratory operations and equipment management.
Train and mentor junior scientists, building technical capability and scientific excellence within the team.
Coordinate with external partners, suppliers, clinical sites, and testing laboratories to support new product development.

Collaboration & Partnership Management
Manage day‑to‑day interactions with internal and external development partners to ensure aligned execution and technical rigor.
Drive consumer centric product science visualization in collaboration with translational science and consumer science teams.

Business, Process & Innovation Support
Manage the product development budget for assigned programs.
Identify opportunities to enhance processes, share knowledge, and strengthen strategic scientific capabilities.

Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s/Master’s degree in Science, Engineering, or Pharmacy with 5+ years of professional R&D experience, or a PhD with 3+ years of professional R&D experience.
Minimum 3 years’ experience in a consumer products organization, with a strong focus on product development and commercialization within OTC or pharmaceutical formulated products.
Strong technical foundation and experience in formulated and engineered products, including tablets, emulsions, surfactants, suspensions, and structured liquids.
Solid understanding of material chemistry and process equipment.
Experience collaborating with manufacturing teams and leading or supporting technical project management activities.
Ability to work effectively in a matrixed organization, building strong cross functional relationships across Marketing, Technology, Formulation, Operations, Regulatory, Medical, and Legal.
Fluent English communication skills (written and verbal) are required.
Agile, proactive, and highly motivated, thriving in fast‑moving environments

Job Description

WHAT YOU’LL DO​
As a Sales Advisor at H&M, you’ll play a key role in creating an outstanding customer experience. You’ll welcome customers, guide them through your store, and support them in finding what they need while showcasing our products. Acting in line with our values, you’ll contribute to both your own success and the success of the company.
You will:
Share your fashion and product knowledge to help customers make informed choices.
Collaborate with your team to deliver exceptional service at every step of the customer journey.
Ensure the sales floor and back of house are well-stocked, organized, and inviting.
Support with opening and closing of the store.
Represent yourself and the brand positively during all customer interactions.

WHO YOU’LL WORK WITH​
Our stores are the heart of our company, where customers experience our brand firsthand. As part of the dynamic Store Team, every role—from Sales Advisors, Department Managers, Store Managers and Visual Merchandisers to Assistant Store Managers, Cash Office Responsible, and Delivery Responsible in larger stores—contributes to creating an inspiring and welcoming environment. You’ll also connect with the wider Area Team, collaborating across stores to share insights and drive success together. Alongside your team, you'll play a vital role in helping customers feel confident and express their individuality with the latest trends and timeless styles. By building meaningful connections with customers in our stores, we make fashion accessible and sustainable for all.
WHO YOU ARE​
We are looking for people with…​
Experience in customer service within fashion, retail, or similar fields.

And people who are…​
Passionate about fashion and delivering an exceptional in-store experience while promoting our products and driving sales.
Thriving in collaborative and dynamic environments.
Communicative, creative, curious to work with store technology, with a strong eagerness to learn and develop.
Flexible and action oriented.

WHO WE ARE​
H&M Group is a global company of strong fashion brands and ventures. Our goal is to prove that there is no compromise between exceptional design, affordable prices, and sustainable solutions. We want to liberate fashion for the many, and our customers are at the heart of every decision we make.​
​We are made up of thousands of passionate and talented colleagues united by our shared culture and values. Together, we want to use our power, our scale, and our knowledge to push the fashion industry towards a more inclusive and sustainable future. ​
WHY YOU’LL LOVE WORKING HERE ​
At H&M Group, we are proud to be a vibrant and welcoming company. We offer our employees attractive benefits with extensive development opportunities around the globe. ​
 All our employees receive a staff discount card, usable on all our H&M Group brands in stores and online. 
In addition to our staff discount, all our employees are included in our H&M Incentive Program – HIP. You can read more about our H&M Incentive Program here. 

JOIN US​
Our uniqueness comes from a combination of many things – our inclusive and collaborative culture, our strong values, and opportunities for growth. But most of all, it’s our people who make us who we are.​
This is a temporary on-demand position with no guaranteed hours. Work will be offered based on business needs with a start in December or by agreement. We are currently looking for people to our store located in Norrtälje and you should be available to work during store opening hours. Language skills in Swedish or English are required.
We have an ongoing selection, so the position may be filled before the application deadline, so send in your application today! The last application date is 2/12.
Take the next step in your career together with us. The journey starts here.​
* Store roles assessment: 
To manage the high volume of applications for the Sales Advisor role, we use an online assessment method for skills-based recruitment within some of our stores. You will need to complete it as part of the application and screening process. Your responses will be scored by an assessment tool that applies predefined criteria set by H&M Group. Please look out for an email in your inbox/junk email from MAKI. 
After completing the assessment, you’ll have the opportunity to share feedback and ask questions. If you experience any difficulties or prefer an alternative assessment method, please contact recruitment_support@hm.com. Choosing an alternative will not impact on your application. 
For more information on how we process your personal data, please see our Privacy Notice. 
** We are committed to a recruitment process that is fair, equitable, and based on competency. We therefore kindly ask you to not attach a cover letter in your application.

jobs.description:
Want to influence the bigger picture? At Saab, you can realise amazing innovations that keep people and societies safe. Together, we can truly make an impact - and your part matters.
Do you want to be part of shaping the future of export control in a world driven by digitalization, cloud technologies, AI, and global collaboration? At Saab, you will contribute to creating safety and security for people and societies while helping build modern, scalable, and future-proof compliance capabilities for tomorrow's technologies.

Your role

Are you interested in international regulations, emerging technologies, and sustainable development? Do you have experience working with product development, digital transformation, or compliance, and are motivated by ensuring that laws and regulations are followed in a rapidly evolving global environment? Then this could be the right role for you.
At Saab, export control is a critical part of our global operations and an essential aspect of our responsibility. As regulations continue to evolve, so does the need to ensure compliance across technologies, data flows, and international collaborations. We are now looking for an Export Control Manager who wants to help shape the future of export control by driving digitalization, smarter ways of working, and modern compliance capabilities within areas such as cloud technologies, AI, and connected systems.
As Export Control Manager, you will have a broad and varied role where you work both operationally and strategically with export control matters. You will support the business through qualified advisory services, manage cases towards relevant authorities, and ensure compliance with applicable export control laws and regulations.
Your responsibilities will include:
Classifying hardware, software, and information in accordance with applicable export control legislation
Supporting projects involving cloud services, AI, digital products, and international collaboration environments from an export control perspective
Driving improvements and modernization of product development processes, systems, and ways of working from an export control perspective
Contributing to digital transformation initiatives and identifying opportunities for automation and smarter compliance processes.
Training and supporting the organization in export control-related matters

The role is varied, collaborative, and at times fast-paced. You will work closely with colleagues across Saab and contribute to building scalable and future-proof export control capabilities.

Your profile

We are looking for someone with experience within export control, compliance, technology, or product development, who feels confident interpreting and applying regulations in complex environments. You hold a relevant academic degree within engineering, law, information technology, or a related field, and you communicate fluently in both Swedish and English, verbally as well as in writing. We also expect you to hold the Certified Export Control Manager (CECM) certification.
You are curious about how new technologies such as AI, cloud solutions, and digital collaboration platforms impact export control and compliance. Experience working with digitalization, process development, or transformation initiatives is highly valued.
As a person, you are analytical, structured, and proactive, with high integrity and a strong sense of responsibility. You enjoy combining operational work with long-term development and are comfortable driving initiatives independently while collaborating closely with others. Experience from defence, high-tech industries, or international environments is considered an advantage.
The person acting in this role shall have the following competence:
Certification "Certified Export Control Manager" or other relevant certification or qualifications.
Knowledge in applicable legal frameworks
Knowledge in export compliance management
Ability to manage and enforce compliance programs
Strong communication and interpersonal skills
Understanding of the prohibitions, restrictions and obligations
Experience in liaising with authorities and regulatory agencies
Analytical and strategic capability to assess and manage compliance risks

This position requires that you pass a security vetting based on the current regulations around/of security protection. For positions requiring security clearance additional obligations on citizenship may apply.

What you will be a part of

Explore a wealth of possibilities. Take on challenges, create smart inventions, and grow beyond. This is a place for curious minds, brave pioneers, and everyone in between. Together, we achieve the extraordinary, each bringing our unique perspectives. Your part matters.
Saab is a leading defense and security company with an enduring purpose, to help nations keep their people and society safe. Empowered by its 28,000 talented people, Saab constantly pushes the boundaries of technology to create a safer and more sustainable world.
Saab designs, manufactures and maintains advanced systems in aeronautics, weapons, command and control, sensors and underwater systems. Saab is headquartered in Sweden. It has major operations all over the world and is part of the domestic defense capability of several nations. Read more about us here

We’re looking for two experienced Fullstack Engineers to join our AML team in Solna. You’ll work with modern cloud-based technology, take ownership of technical decisions and help develop one of our most strategically important products.
About us
At Verified, we build cloud-based solutions for identity verification, electronic signing and Anti-Money Laundering (AML). Our platform supports AML/KYC, supplier due diligence and secure digital workflows.
We’re around 100 people, mainly serving the Nordic market, with a user network that spans Europe. Our API-first platform lets businesses integrate secure, scalable services into their existing systems and workflows.
Technology is at the heart of what we do, and we keep investing in cloud infrastructure, scalable architecture and AI-driven solutions. Our engineers work in autonomous, cross-functional teams with shared ownership, a strong engineering culture and a real say in how our products and technology evolve.
The role and the team
As a Senior Fullstack Engineer, you’ll help develop and scale our cloud-based AML platform. You’ll work across frontend, backend and cloud infrastructure, with significant influence over architecture and technical decisions.
You’ll join an experienced team of three senior Fullstack Engineers and work closely with our Product Owner, Designer, QA and Engineering Manager. The team has a high degree of autonomy and owns the full development lifecycle, from system design and implementation to deployment and operations.
Our stack is mainly Node.js and TypeScript on the backend, Vue.js on the frontend, and AWS and MongoDB Atlas for cloud infrastructure and data storage. The platform is API-first, with a strong focus on scalability, security and performance.
In the role, you will:

Design and develop scalable cloud-based systems, REST APIs and modern web applications.

Contribute to architecture and technical decisions, improving scalability and reducing system dependencies.

Build integrations, manage complex data flows and improve system reliability.

Drive engineering quality through testing, code reviews, CI/CD and troubleshooting.

Use AI agents and automated workflows to improve our products and development processes.

AI is an important investment area for us. We’re continuously looking for ways to improve how we use AI and to stay up to date with new tools and practices, so you’ll have the chance to shape how AI is used across the development lifecycle and built into our products.
We see software engineering as a craft, where technical quality, thoughtful decisions and pragmatic solutions go hand in hand.
What will you bring to the team?
You’re an experienced Fullstack Engineer who enjoys solving complex challenges, taking ownership and contributing to technical decisions. You’re comfortable working independently while collaborating closely with other engineers and product stakeholders.
We think you have:

At least five years of experience in fullstack development, preferably in cloud-based SaaS environments.

Strong experience with Node.js, TypeScript and modern frontend frameworks.

Experience building REST APIs and working with distributed or API-first systems.

Hands-on experience with cloud platforms, preferably AWS.

A good understanding of system design, security and modern application architecture.

Experience with, or an interest in, AI tools and modern development workflows.

Professional proficiency in English and the right to work in Sweden.

It’s a plus if you have experience from FinTech, RegTech or other regulated industries, or with third-party integrations, or if you speak Swedish.
As a person, you’re curious, self-driven and comfortable taking responsibility for what you build. You enjoy technical discussions, sharing knowledge and finding practical solutions that balance quality, performance and business needs.
What we offer
With us, you’ll work on technology that helps businesses prevent financial crime and meet increasingly complex regulatory requirements. You’ll join an experienced engineering team with significant influence over architecture, technical decisions and development practices, and you’ll help shape how we use AI and modern technologies across Verified.

Significant influence over technical decisions and product development.

An experienced team with a high degree of autonomy and shared ownership.

Modern cloud technology and AI-driven development.

30 days of vacation, plus five “Verified days” for bridge days and holiday flexibility.

Wellness allowance and occupational pension.

A hybrid model and prefer working together from our Solna office 2-3 days per week.

Office breakfasts and snacks, social activities and one moving day per year.

Other information
Start: According to agreement 

Extent: Full time

Location: Our Stockholm office in Solna

The recruitment process
We review applications on an ongoing basis, so don’t wait to apply!
We’re running this recruitment together with our partner Detechtiv. If you have any questions about the role or the process, contact Jonathan at Jonathan@detechtiv.se.
Our selection process is continuous, and the advert may close before the recruitment process is completed if we have moved forward to the screening or interview phase.

You will be responsible for delivering professional and high-quality customer communication across our B2C brands, primarily supporting customers in the Nordic markets. Through email support, customer feedback and public reviews, you will help build trust, strengthen our brand and ensure a consistent customer experience.
We are looking for someone who is an excellent communicator, detail-oriented and genuinely interested in creating positive customer experiences. You understand the importance of tone of voice, brand consistency and putting the customer first in every interaction.
This is a 12-month fixed-term opportunity at 50%, ideal for someone looking for a flexible part-time role alongside another job, studies or other commitments.
What You'll Do
Be the voice of Albert: Communicate with customers in a professional and brand-aligned way, ensuring every interaction reflects our values and tone of voice.
Deliver excellent customer support: Handle customer inquiries primarily via email, including subscriptions, payments, renewals and cancellations.
Represent our brand externally: Monitor and respond to customer reviews and feedback on platforms such as Trustpilot, the App Store and Google Play.
Ensure quality and consistency: Pay close attention to detail, accuracy and clarity in all customer-facing communication.
Identify customer insights: Recognise recurring questions, feedback and potential issues, and share relevant insights with the team.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders: Share customer insights, feedback and recurring issues with relevant teams, including Legal, Marketing and Tech, helping improve the overall customer experience.
Support brand communication: Help maintain and improve our Help Center and other customer-facing content, ensuring consistent messaging across channels.
Follow established processes: Handle customer information responsibly and follow internal guidelines and procedures.
Drive continuous improvement: Proactively identify opportunities to improve how we work with customer support, including processes, response templates and the overall customer experience. Bring forward ideas and take initiative to make our support more efficient and customer-focused.

Who You Are
An excellent communicator with strong written skills in both Swedish and English. Other Nordic languages are a plus.
Brand-conscious and confident in adapting your tone of voice to different customers and situations.
Service-minded, detail-oriented and quality-focused, with a genuine interest in creating positive customer experiences.
Driven, curious and proactive. You identify opportunities for improvement, share ideas and take initiative.
Responsible and comfortable working independently, quick to learn new systems and digital tools, and confident collaborating with different teams and stakeholders.
Flexible and able to adapt your working hours based on changing business needs throughout the year.

Meriting Experience
Previous experience in customer service, communication or a similar role.
Experience working with GDPR, data privacy or handling personal data.
Basic knowledge of data protection and privacy regulations.
Experience with customer support platforms or digital tools.

About Albert
At Albert, our vision is to ensure that every child around the world has access to a tailored and engaging learning experience.
Together with a passionate and talented team, we create educational games that combine world-class content, data, and technology to help children develop their mathematical and linguistic skills in a fun and meaningful way. By personalizing learning for each individual user, we aim to make education more accessible, effective, and inspiring – regardless of age.
We are a fast-paced scale-up where the distance between idea and decision is short. Curiosity and innovation are at the core of everything we do, and we believe meaningful work is best done in an environment that encourages joy, creativity, and collaboration.

What We Offer
The opportunity to work towards a meaningful mission and help shape the future of learning.
A collaborative environment with skilled, curious and passionate colleagues.
Empowered teams with high autonomy and strong support.
An open culture that values innovation, learning and knowledge sharing, including contributions to open source.
Competitive benefits, including a monthly pension contribution and social activities.
A hybrid working setup with flexible working hours.
The opportunity to gain hands-on experience in customer support, brand communication and customer experience while working with colleagues across different countries and teams.
The possibility to combine this role with another job, studies or other commitments.

Employment Details

Work arrangement: Hybrid, with flexible working hours.

jobs.occupation: Embedded Firmware Engineer within video streaming
jobs.description:
About the role
Wrknest Engineering is recruiting for a global tech company, and we are now looking for an Embedded Firmware Engineer to join the team behind its video surveillance product. The product is one of the fastest growing parts of a wider ecosystem that covers networking, surveillance, VoIP and access control.
In this role, video is at the heart of everything you do. You will work on the firmware running on the cameras themselves, from bootloader up to user space, with a strong focus on video and audio streaming, transcoding and performance on ARM-based platforms. The code base is almost entirely C++, and your work ends up in products used by businesses and homes all over the world.
You will join a highly product-driven environment where small teams own their products, with real ownership over technical decisions. The company combines the pace and mindset of a startup with the reach of a global tech company. You will work closely with hardware, backend, frontend, mobile, QA and manufacturing to make sure every device works flawlessly in the field.
Your main responsibilities

Implement kernel mode and user mode applications for the device firmware, from bootloader up to user-space applications, including Linux Kernel, rootfs, Websocket, RESTful API design and gRPC

Develop and optimize video and audio streaming and transcoding on embedded devices

Implement features to support hardware testing and diagnosis of various embedded devices

Work closely with teams such as EE, Backend, Frontend, Mobile, QA, Factory and Manufacturing

We are looking for you who have

Proficiency in C++ (the code base is about 99 % C++) and C

Proficiency with video and audio streaming as well as transcoding

Understanding of and experience with ARM platforms

Experience with debuggers such as gdb and strace

Embedded software development experience in Linux drivers, in both kernel and user mode

Familiarity with scripting (shell, Python, Node.js)

Familiarity with Git version control

A genuine passion for embedded software development

A self-motivated, goal-driven team player who loves difficult challenges and can deliver on tight schedules

A BSc/MSc in Computer Engineering, Computer Science or equivalent

Fluency in written and spoken English to work effectively with colleagues around the world

Nice to have

Familiarity with Sigmastar or Ambarella platforms

Experience with development boards such as Raspberry Pi, Arduino or BeagleBoard

Experience with build systems such as OpenWRT, BuildRoot or Yocto

Department of Aquatic Resources (SLU Aqua)
We are seeking a highly-motivated researcher in fisheries stock assessment at the Department of Aquatic Resources for a part-time position (75%), starting in February 2027. The researcher will contribute to development of the stock assessment for Atlantic salmon in the Baltic Sea, and potentially other salmonid species, as well as participating in international research projects. This position will have a focus on developing and implementing Bayesian statistical models, so prior experience in this field is required.
About the position
The ICES Baltic salmon and trout assessment working group (WGBAST) conducts an annual stock assessment that serves as the basis for catch advice for salmon stocks in the Baltic Sea using an MSY (maximum sustainable yield) approach. The stock assessment consists of a state-space Bayesian modelling framework that integrates multiple data sources at different life stages. This assessment framework is currently undergoing a process of development and review, and we are seeking a researcher who can contribute to this work. At the same time, the new researcher will contribute to ongoing research projects that are linked to the stock assessment.
Tasks
Contribute to the stock assessment and basis for scientific advice for Atlantic salmon in the Baltic Sea (developing and implementing Bayesian statistical models).
Improving the biological realism of stock assessment models (analysing life-history trait data and incorporating spatio-temporal variation in life-history traits to stock assessment models).
Participation in international expert groups.
Participate in and contribute to ongoing research projects within the Institute for Freshwater Research. Examples include BAYeFISH, a project aimed at improving inference of juvenile fish density using hierarchical Bayesian models, and diadPATH, a new EU Horizon project that will support more holistic assessment methods for diadromous fish species (accounting for effects of hydropower and climate change, increased biological realism and improved fisheries reference points for status evaluation).
The successful candidate is also expected to publish scientific articles and apply for their own research funding.

The researcher will be based at SLU’s Institute of Freshwater Research near Stockholm. The Institute of Freshwater Research offers a stimulating work environment, with a dedicated research group on diadromous fish species (including eel and salmon stock assessment). In addition, the researcher will have access to a wider international research network through the EU diadPATH project.

jobs.description:

Om jobbet
Potter Clarkson is a leading pan-European intellectual property law firm, with offices across the UK, Denmark, Sweden and Germany. We provide a full range of intellectual property services, supporting clients in achieving their commercial objectives and protecting their innovations and brands.
Our Stockholm office is a growing part of the firm and we are looking for a talented, organised and proactive Trade Mark Paralegal to join the team.
This is an excellent opportunity for someone with strong administrative and organisational skills who is looking to build their career within Trade Marks. Previous intellectual property experience would be advantageous, but we are equally interested in candidates who can demonstrate the right skills, attitude and willingness to learn.
The role
As a Trade Mark Paralegal, you will play an important role in supporting the management of Trade Mark portfolios and providing high-quality support to our attorneys and clients.
This is a varied and fast-paced role involving the preparation of Trade Mark registry documentation, client reporting, correspondence with Trade Mark registries and the accurate maintenance of case records and deadlines.
Working closely with professional staff and colleagues across the firm, you will also liaise with clients, overseas attorneys and other legal firms around the world.
Being part of our Stockholm office will give you the opportunity to contribute to a growing local team while benefiting from the knowledge, infrastructure and support of a wider European IP practice.
Key responsibilities
Your responsibilities will include:
Preparing Trade Mark registry forms and associated documentation.
Preparing reports and updates for clients.
Corresponding with Trade Mark registries and other relevant intellectual property offices.
Processing and docketing incoming correspondence.
Maintaining accurate and up-to-date case records on the firm's systems.
Monitoring and managing deadlines and ensuring appropriate action is taken within the required timescales.
Liaising with attorneys and other professional staff regarding client matters.
Liaising professionally with clients, overseas attorneys, other legal firms and external parties.
Supporting the management of Trade Mark portfolios.
Assisting with the preparation and maintenance of client and internal documentation.
Providing additional administrative and paralegal support to the team as required.

About you
You will be highly organised and comfortable working in a busy professional environment where accuracy and meeting deadlines are essential.
We are looking for someone who can demonstrate:
Strong administrative and organisational skills.
Excellent attention to detail and the ability to complete work to a high standard.
The ability to manage and prioritise your own workload effectively.
Good interpersonal and communication skills, with a proactive and personable approach.
A professional manner when communicating with clients and other external parties.
The ability to work independently as well as collaboratively as part of a team.
A conscientious, motivated and flexible approach to work.
Strong IT skills, including a good working knowledge of Microsoft Office.
The ability and enthusiasm to learn new systems, processes and areas of intellectual property.
The ability to work effectively under pressure and manage competing deadlines.
Fluency in written and spoken English
Strong communication skills in Swedish

Desirable experience and qualifications
It would be advantageous if you have:
Previous experience within Trade Marks or intellectual property would be advantageous
Knowledge of IP management systems, Trade Mark legislation, rules or procedures.
A relevant Trade Mark paralegal, IP administration or equivalent professional qualification.

These are desirable rather than essential, and training and support will be provided to develop your knowledge and skills.
Why join Potter Clarkson?
Joining our Stockholm office offers the opportunity to be part of a growing local team while enjoying the resources and opportunities available within an established pan-European intellectual property firm.
We offer a supportive, friendly and collaborative working environment and are committed to investing in the development of our people.
We can offer:
The benefits of a smaller, growing office combined with the infrastructure of a larger European firm.
The opportunity to work with colleagues and clients internationally.
Exposure to varied and interesting Trade Mark work.
Opportunities for continued professional development and learning.
A collaborative working environment where you can contribute ideas and make an impact.
A strong commitment to work-life balance and employee wellbeing.

Potter Clarkson is committed to providing a supportive, inclusive and stimulating workplace for all our people.
Benefits
Competitive salary based on experience.
Flexible working arrangements.
Pension scheme.
Healthcare benefits.
Support for health and wellbeing.
Regular company away days and social events.
Opportunities for professional development.

A Snapshot of Your Day
As a Solutions Engineer you will work at the intersection of technology, customer needs, and project execution. One day, you might support a bid team in suggesting a surface treatment solution for a new turbine project. The next, you could be collaborating with suppliers, engineering, and service colleagues to resolve a technical challenge or improve an existing standard.
Working closely with an experienced colleague, you will contribute to projects throughout their lifecycle, from the early sales phase to delivery and service support. Through your technical expertise and customer focus, you will help ensure reliable and sustainable solutions for our customers worldwide.
About the Role
As a Solutions Engineer specializing in Surface Treatment, you will provide technical knowledge in coatings, corrosion protection, and surface treatment technologies for our products and projects.
You will support bid and delivery projects, contribute to technical evaluations and standardization activities, and provide guidance to internal stakeholders, suppliers, and customers. The role offers broad exposure across engineering, sales, quality, and service functions, providing a unique opportunity to build both technical depth and business understanding.
The role also includes site- and supplier visits, technical support, investigations and inspections.
Working alongside experienced colleagues, you will continuously develop your expertise while helping to drive quality, innovation, and continuous improvement within your field. As your experience grows, you pave the way for future opportunities.
Your Responsibilities
Support sales teams with technical input for quotations and specifications.
Support the development of project-specific surface treatment specifications.
Provide technical support for standard solutions and customer adaptations.
Assist in technical discussions with suppliers, customers, and internal stakeholders.
Maintain technical documentation, procedures, and specifications.
Support service projects and site activities.
Review technical documentation, datasheets, and supplier proposals.
Structuring and development of current surface treatment related documents

What You Bring
A relevant education/background within surface treatment or a similar field.
Experience within surface treatment or a similar field.
Experience with gas turbine products and a good understanding of Extended Scope / Balance of Plant.
Good communication skills in English, both written and spoken.
A structured and quality-focused mindset.
A genuine interest in customer issues and in solving the customer’s challenges
A collaborative approach with a willingness to learn and develop.

What We Offer
An excellent opportunity to develop expertise within surface treatment and corrosion protection.
Mentorship and support from experienced engineering professionals.
Exposure to international projects and advanced energy technologies.
A collaborative environment focused on innovation, quality, and continuous improvement.
Opportunities for professional growth within Siemens Energy.

About the team
Join a team of 11 talented professionals with diverse backgrounds and expertise. We work across a wide range of disciplines, from front-end engineering and development engineering to business development. What unites us is a strong team spirit and a willingness to support one another.
Our Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet.
We can offer you employment benefits such as: reduction of working hours, advance vacation, health care allowance and an eventual possibility to a flexible working place.
Who is Siemens Energy?
At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100,000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation. 
Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity, we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Would you like to take ownership of global trade compliance in an international, technology-driven environment? As Global Trade Compliance (GTC) Manager at Silex, you will develop our export control processes and help colleagues navigate trade compliance requirements in their daily work. With our headquarters and manufacturing operations in Sweden and ambitious expansion plans in the United States, you will play a key role in supporting our continued international growth.
Would you like to know more about Silex and what we do? Read more here.
In this role, you will:

Lead and develop global trade compliance, with a focus on export controls, sanctions, and international trade regulations, including US requirements.

Work with export controls under the Wassenaar Arrangement as a central part of the role, translating requirements into practical processes and guidance.

Coordinate export license applications and regulatory matters with authorities, including the Swedish Inspectorate of Strategic Products (ISP).

Oversee customer and end-use screening, export classifications, and compliance records in close collaboration with technical and commercial teams.

Read and assess trade compliance requirements in customer and supplier agreements, identifying export control implications and supporting internal decision-making.

Develop and maintain trade compliance processes, guidelines, and documentation, and update procedures as requirements evolve.

Train and guide colleagues on export control and trade compliance, making complex requirements clear and actionable.

We are looking for someone who has:

Extensive experience working with global trade compliance in a technology-driven industrial company.

The ability to read and understand agreements and identify requirements relevant to export control and trade compliance.

A structured approach and the ability to translate complex trade compliance requirements into clear, practical business guidance.

Excellent communication skills in both Swedish and English, written and spoken.

Experience working with export controls under the Wassenaar Arrangement. This is highly valued, but not a strict requirement; it will be a central part of your work in this role.

Technical understanding that helps you assess products, processes, and related export control requirements.

Experience from an international company and with export controls related to the United States.

You take initiative, bring structure, and are as comfortable getting things done yourself as you are developing better ways of working. You enjoy collaborating and make complex matters easy to understand.
What we offer you:

Close collaboration with management and specialist colleagues.

The opportunity to take ownership of and shape our global trade compliance processes and ways of working.

A key role supporting a leading technology company’s international growth.

Knowledge exchange with technical experts, connecting advanced MEMS technology with export control and trade compliance.

jobs.description:
Shape the future of information security at ASSA ABLOY! Strengthen security and compliance across the Nordic region.
Are you ready to make a real impact on information security in a global organization?At ASSA ABLOY, you will strengthen security governance, risk management and compliance across the Nordic Business Area. Working with security specialists and business stakeholders, you will translate security requirements into practical improvements.Combining strategic influence with hands-on responsibility, you will work across complex IT and OT environments, supported by an international team and strong management commitment.
The Opportunity
Information security is business critical at ASSA ABLOY. As Nordic operations move towards more unified security practices, you will help align requirements, strengthen collaboration and improve security maturity across countries.
You will join a collaborative Security team and influence how security is implemented across the business. ASSA ABLOY is the global leader in access solutions, with nearly 63,000 colleagues in more than 70 countries.
Your Challenge
As Information Security Compliance Manager, you will develop and implement a unified approach to security governance and compliance across the Nordic Business Area. You will work hands-on with audits, risk assessments and controls, translating standards and regulations into practical solutions.
Your key responsibilities include:
Strengthen security governance, processes and controls across Nordic operations.
Implement and maintain security practices aligned with ISO 27001, IEC 62443, NIS2, CRA and relevant protective security requirements.
Plan, conduct and follow up on internal, external and third-party security audits, driving remediation with technical teams.
Develop supplier security risk management, assessing new suppliers and prioritizing existing suppliers based on risk.
Conduct hands-on security assessments across IT and OT environments, production sites and critical suppliers.
Develop security policies, guidelines and awareness initiatives to strengthen security culture.
Participate in security incident response, preparedness, recovery and lessons learned.
Monitor security KPIs and KRIs, report to management and advise stakeholders across IT, procurement, legal and business.

You will have the opportunity to challenge existing approaches, take ownership and make a tangible difference to security across the Nordic organization.
The Team and Workplace
You will join an international Security team with colleagues across the Nordic region, including Sweden, Denmark and Finland. Collaboration is mainly digital, with the team aiming to meet in person approximately once a month.
The position can be based in Sweden, Finland, Norway, Denmark or Estonia. The general guideline is three office days per week, with individual flexibility.
You will report to the Head of Risk Management and Security for the Nordic Business Area.
About You
We are looking for an information security professional combining governance, risk and compliance expertise with a practical, business-oriented approach. Your background may be in information security, cybersecurity, GRC or a related field. Hands-on experience and the ability to deliver improvements matter more than a specific number of years in the profession.
We believe you bring:
Practical experience in information security, risk management and compliance.
Applied knowledge of ISO 27001 and relevant standards and regulations, including IEC 62443, NIS2 and CRA.
Experience implementing controls, conducting audits and following up on security risks.
Understanding of IT and OT environments and industrial security challenges.
Ability to translate security requirements into workable business solutions.
Strong collaboration, communication and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work independently across teams and countries, with strong written and spoken English.

Experience implementing ISO 27001 in a larger organization is particularly valuable. ISO 27001 Lead Auditor certification, protective security knowledge and experience from manufacturing, technology or critical infrastructure are advantages.
Relevant education, certifications or equivalent practical experience are welcome.
You are curious, pragmatic and proactive. You build trust, take initiative and find solutions when answers are not obvious. You enjoy combining structure with hands-on work and collaborating across different functions and backgrounds.
Security requirements: The position requires a personal security pre-employment check, security interview and evaluation in accordance with the Swedish Protective Security Act (Säkerhetsskyddslagen 2018:585). The assessment takes place after the recruitment selection process and before an employment offer.
